text.p: The chief executive of Norddeutsche Landesbank (NordLB) said late on Wednesday that talks on a link-up between NordLB and Bankgesellschaft AG would not start in earnest until 1997.
Manfred Bodin told a news conference that the outcome of those talks was still completely open.
Bodin said he believed that a link-up between the two banks would make sense only in certain business areas like investment banking or corporate finance.

In a move which fuelled speculation about mergers in Germany's overcrowded banking sector, the two banks in October got the go-ahead from their owners -- several federal states in northern and eastern Germany -- to intensify talks about increasing co-operation.
Bodin said the management boards of the two banks were currently reviewing organisational and legal aspects of a link-up.
The banks had made progress in reviewing possibilities to cooperate in their international activities and to set up a joint subsidiary for securities transaction settlement, Bodin said.
They were also cooperating closely in preparing for European monetary union.

He added that the talks were not affected by Bankgesellschaft's announcement last week that it would set aside a 2.2 billion-mark provision for credit risks. Bankgesellschaft is a healthy bank, Bodin said.
